ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the following lists: (1) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, (2) the U.S. Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, (3) the European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, (4) the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit's list of designated persons under the Act on Reporting and Use of Specified Financial Transaction Information, and (5) the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) public statements on high-risk and non-cooperative jurisdictions. Additionally, a Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) check must be conducted using a reputable commercial database, with enhanced due diligence required for any PEP, family member, or close associate. The screening must be performed at onboarding, on a continuous basis (at least quarterly), and upon any material change in ownership or control. All results must be documented and retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Internet Registration Office (I-REG) of the Korean Court Registry (https://www.iros.go.kr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in Korean script (Hangul). If a foreign name is used, it must be transliterated into Hangul phonetically. The name must include a legal form indicator such as '유한회사' (Yuhan Hoesa) for a limited liability company. The name must be distinguishable from existing registered names and must not contain any prohibited or sensitive tokens. The four-tier naming convention requires: (1) the name must be unique within the same jurisdiction, (2) it must not be identical or confusingly similar to existing trademarks or trade names, (3) it must not include any terms that imply a government affiliation or regulated industry without prior approval, and (4) it must be in compliance with the Korean Commercial Act and the Act on the Registration of Real Estate and Other Matters.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, Act No. 1000, promulgated December 31, 1962, as amended, specifically Articles 287-1 to 287-74 (Yuhan Hoesa/LLC), Article 292 (Articles of Incorporation), Article 317 (Incorporation Registration), Article 635 (Penal Provisions for False Registration), supplemented by the Foreign Investment Promotion Act Articles 2, 5, 6 and 27 (foreign-invested enterprise reporting) and the Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Guarantee of Confidentiality (bank account verification).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Supreme Court Registration Bureau via the local District Court Registry Office (Dunsan-dong, or competent civil registry division of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office of the company).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation Registration Application (beob-in-seol-rip-deung-gi-shin-cheong-seo), Articles of Incorporation (jeong-gwan), and filed Notarized Minutes of the Initial Members/Shareholders Meeting.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under the Commercial Act. The Yuhan Hoesa has no statutory minimum paid-in capital. All member contributions, regardless of par value, must be fully paid in cash or in kind before the registration application is filed. There is no escrow or blocked account requirement under Korean company law; however, where foreign funds are introduced, a foreign investment report must be lodged with a designated foreign exchange bank, and capital may be remitted through the bank's Foreign Investment Account before the registry filing. The Articles of Incorporation must state each member's contribution value and the method of contribution.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS / MEMBERS OF YUHAN HOESA (LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY) NUMBERED RESOLUTION 2026-001 

1. ADOPTION AND CONFIRMATION OF INCORPORATION. The Board of Directors of Yuhan Hoesa, having been duly constituted on [Date], resolves that the incorporation of the Company under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea is hereby ratified and confirmed, and that the Articles of Incorporation, including the corporate name, registered office, business purpose, total number of contributed units, and contribution amounts, are accepted as the governing organic documents of the Company. 

2. CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND CONTRIBUTION. That each member appearing on the equity schedule shall pay the contribution set forth opposite their name, and that such contributions are fully subscribed and either duly paid into the Company's domestic bank account or lawfully contributed in kind, and that the Chief Executive Officer shall obtain and preserve all contribution remittance receipts and contribution valuation reports. 

3. BANKING AUTHORIZATION AND SIGNATORY DESIGNATION. That the Company shall open ordinary banking accounts, foreign exchange accounts, and any payment collection accounts with a financial institution in the Republic of Korea; that the Chief Executive Officer, the Chief Financial Officer, and any two directors jointly shall be authorized to open, operate, and close such accounts; and that all payment service agreements with TikTok, Wise, and any connected payout platforms shall require dual signatory approval above KRW 50,000,000 equivalents. 

4. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. That the registered office located at [Insert Full Address, Seoul/Other Jurisdiction, Republic of Korea] is hereby adopted as the sole administrative head office and legal seat of the Company; that a registered agent is appointed for service of process; and that the necessary lease agreement, landlord's consent, and occupancy documentation be filed with the registration authorities. 

5. OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. That [Name] is appointed Chief Executive Officer, [Name] is appointed Chief Financial Officer, and [Name] is appointed Corporate Secretary, with statutory duties, authority, and liability as provided under the Commercial Act; each appointee accepts office and shall submit their consent and identity documentation. 

6. DELEGATION AND AUTHORITY. That the officers are delegated authority to execute all registration forms, tax filings, bank forms, foreign investment filings, and operating certificates required to carry the Company into full legal existence and regulatory compliance. 

7. GENERAL. That any resolution, act, or document necessary to implement the foregoing is approved, and the Corporate Secretary is directed to file and publish this resolution in the corporate minute book.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Name Verification, Articles of Incorporation Drafting, and Foreign Investment Report Preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court Internet Registration Office (IRO) for name search and reservation; Korean Intellectual Property Office for corporate name similarity; designated foreign exchange bank for foreign investment report if non-resident owns interest.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a corporate name availability search on the Supreme Court IRO and reserve the Korean legal name 'Yuhan Hoesa' with a unique trade name. Prepare the full Articles of Incorporation in Korean, specifying the exact ISIC 7310 advertising agency and creator management business purpose, registered office location, contribution amounts, member names, and officer provisions. If a member is a non-resident, prepare a Foreign Investment Report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, submit the report to a designated foreign exchange bank, and obtain a Foreign Investment Registration Certificate. All documents must be notarized at a notary public licensed by the Ministry of Justice. Exact authorities are the District Prosecutors' office for notary commissions and the designated bank for foreign exchange. Adverse action remedy: if name is rejected due to identical or confusingly similar existing name, immediately amend the proposed name and re-submit; no standing fees are lost if reserve within 30 days. SLA: 2 business days for name reservation; 3 business days for foreign investment report review.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID of each member
Business plan or intended business scope statement
Proposed official Korean corporate name
Foreign investment report form and passport if non-resident
Articles of Incorporation draft
Power of attorney for formation agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the foreign investment report is queried, submit supplementary explanation of the source of funds and the ISIC/NAICS business scope to the foreign exchange bank; if name is objectionable, file a fresh name search and amend Articles immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Contributions and Opening of the Domestic Capital Contribution Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank authorized to handle foreign exchange transactions in Korea (e.g. KEB Hana Bank, Woori Bank, Shinhan Bank, or any bank with Foreign Exchange Business License).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional company account or subscription deposit account with the chosen bank. Receive the full cash contribution from each member by wire or in-person deposit into the account and ensure the name of the depositor matches the member's name. Upon payment, obtain a contribution deposit certificate or bank-issued confirmation stating the account number, deposit date, and total amount. For in-kind contributions, arrange independent evaluation by a certified public accountant per Commercial Act Article 290 and append the valuation report. After the deposit certificate is received, the directors must maintain a copy for the 14-day newspaper/public notice procedure if in-kind contributions are used. No minimum capital applies, but every contributed unit must be fully paid. Adverse action remedy: if the bank refuses opening due to unresolved source-of-funds questions, provide certified proof of lawful origin and a transaction declaration; if the name on deposit differs from the member, correct via bank amendment form before registration. SLA: 2 business days.
required_dossiers: Company formation operational instructions
Identity documents of all contributors
Foreign Investment Registration Certificate or pre-registration slip, if applicable
Draft Articles of Incorporation with contribution schedule
Bank's anti-money laundering questionnaire and beneficial owner declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank imposes enhanced due diligence, provide tax residence documentation and declaring the ultimate beneficial owner; the account is not an escrow but must be a real domestic account in the Company's name before final registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Articles of Incorporation and Filing of the Incorporation Registration Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public (beopmu-sa in the district of the Company's registered office) then the local District Court Registry Office (Registration Division).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Each original Article of Incorporation is signed or sealed by the members and notarized before the competent notary. Thereafter, the directors or their appointed legal representative submit the incorporation registration application to the Local District Court Registry Office having territorial jurisdiction. The application must include the notarized Articles, Certificate of Deposit of Contributions, documents concerning appointed officers, the registered office lease or title documents, and the court form for corporation incorporation registration. The registry will examine whether the company name, purpose, capital, and officers are lawful; upon approval, a Certificate of Registration will be issued. Adverse action remedy: if the court issues a correction order (bogwan), correct within the grace period using the court's specified superseding document and pay any additional surcharge if the 14-day statutory registration period has passed. SLA: 4 business days.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation (notarized copy)
Incorporation registration application (court form)
Bank Certificate of Contribution Deposit
Certificate of Officer Consent and appointment acceptance
Landlord's consent or lease agreement for the registered office
Power of attorney if represented by a service provider
Incorporation registration fee payment receipt (court stamp due to small-value stamp)
For foreign investors: Foreign Investment Registration Certificate copy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is suspended for ambiguity in business purpose, file an amended scope referencing 'advertising and creator MCN agency, ISIC 7310'; if the certificate of contribution is insufficient, obtain a re-issued bank statement and re-submit before the 21st day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration with the National Tax Service and Local Government Post-Incorporation Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Competent District Tax Office of the National Tax Service (district tax office governing the registered office jurisdiction); relevant local government for municipal business taxes.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 20 calendar days of the court registration, file the Business Registration Certificate application for corporate income tax and value-added tax with the competent District Tax Office. The application must state the official corporate name, Employers' Registration Number, head office address, business purpose sticker code for advertising agencies under Korean Standard Industrial Classification corresponding to ISIC 7310, and legal representative details. Following the District Tax Office approval, the Company obtains the corporate business registration certificate and VAT invoice privileges. The Company must additionally register for Local Income Tax and business license with the local municipal government. This step is also triggered for any required VAT registrations for creator payout income. Adverse action remedy: if the tax office flags mismatch with the corporate registration, provide a certified copy of court registration and file a correction under the Framework Act on National Taxes; if late, pay minor punitive surcharge but no dissolution risk. SLA: 3 business days.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Corporation Registration from the court
Articles of Incorporation
Business registration application form (NTS form)
Lease or occupancy proof
Identification and endorsements of directors
Corporate seal certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NTS rejects the business purpose code, submit a comparative table matching NAICS 541810 and Korean Industry Classification 7310 'Advertising' plus 'Internet advertisements and digital creator support'; if a prior corporate entity has same trade name, select a suffix.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Governance Startup Formalities: Board Minutes, Banking Activation, and Insurance/Social Security Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company Directors, the Company's corporate bank, and the National Pension Service / Korea Workers' Compensation & Welfare Service / National Health Insurance Service as applicable for employees.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify the first Board Resolution has been entered into the corporate minute book; take the certificate of incorporation and corporate seal to the bank to convert the provisional contribution account into a fully operational corporate account. Execute TIER operations for TikTok Creator Payout via Wise or direct SWIFT, meaning create the company beneficiary profile with the Korean corporate bank, secure API or bank keys for payouts, and ensure strict separation of director-held personal accounts. For each employee and externally engaged creator paid under employment or supplier contract, register the company with the four major social insurance systems: National Pension, National Health Insurance, Employment Insurance, and Industrial Accident Compensation Insurance. If office space is physical, separately apply for the Fire Safety Certificate through the local fire department and the Hazard Prevention Certificate under the Occupational Safety and Health Act if workplace has five or more employees. Adverse action remedy: for non-approval of payout account API, file corrected CBDC domestic transaction report and add second signatory; for insurance registration failure, use the electronic joint portal of the National Pension Service and resolve within ten days. SLA: 7 business days.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution minutes
Certificate of incorporation
Corporate seal certificate
Bank account opening forms and ultimate beneficial owner declarations
Employment contract and social insurance registration list
Lease agreement and floor plan for fire safety application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires additional anti-money laundering documents, provide source of payout receivable report and contractual agreements with TikTok; for insurance, appeal through the Social Insurance Reconsideration Committee in the jurisdiction.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - pure digital media advertising agency and multi-channel network (MCN) service without physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or warehousing operations under ISIC 7310/NAICS 541810.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no manufacturing operation license, no factory establishment permit, no import/export customs license reserved for physical goods is required for the main activity.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea (with KECO enforcement under the Environmental Affairs Act).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - classification is Exempt from Environmental Impact Assessment and Environmental Registration because the registered activity is pure digital advertising and creator management with no point-source emission, no wastewater discharge, and no physical production site.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no wastewater discharge, no VOC emission volatility, no hazardous waste stream, and no combustion unit. If the company later opens a physical studio, warehouse, or studio-manufacturing facility, the operation must be reclassified and a notice of business under the Clean Air Conservation Act and Water Environment Conservation Act would be separately filed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable to the core digital operation. If the company leases an office, the lessor must maintain fire safety certification under the Fire Protection and Prevention of Fire Hazards to Protect the Human Environment Act, and the company must secure a routine fire-prevention inspection by the municipal fire department, a structural load certificate from the building owner, and a workplace safety certificate under the Occupational Safety and Health Act prior to staffing the office with regular employees. No industrial civil-defense clearance is required because there is no physical factory or warehouse, but a simple fire drill log and designated evacuation officer are required under the Fire Safety Act.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; electronic portal: NTS HomeTax (https://www.hometax.go.kr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident establishing a Yuhan Hoesa (Korean limited liability company) must obtain a Korean Business Registration Number (BRN; the 10-digit taxpayer identification number) from the NTS district tax office having jurisdiction over the principal place of business. Procedure: (1) complete Korean court registration of the Yuhan Hoesa and, if needed, appoint a domestic statutory tax representative for the foreign shareholders; (2) before or within 20 days after business commencement, file the Business Registration Application with the competent district tax office or through HomeTax, attaching the certificate of incorporation, corporate registration certificate, Korean office lease or rental proof, foreign director identification and apostilled corporate documents, and a tax representative appointment power of attorney; (3) receive the 10-digit BRN, which also serves as the VAT registration number, corporate income tax payer ID, and employer withholding tax ID; (4) register in HomeTax for electronic tax invoice issuance, cash receipt card issuance, and direct debit VAT payment. A foreign supplier with no Korean place of business that is nevertheless required to charge Korean VAT on services used in Korea must register through a Korean tax representative on HomeTax and obtain a BRN before issuing tax invoices.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korean tax law does not provide a check-the-box or pass-through election for a Yuhan Hoesa. The entity is a domestic corporation subject to entity-level taxation under the Corporate Income Tax Act, and no hybrid mismatch elections are available under Korean domestic law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary threshold. VAT registration is mandatory at business commencement for every business operator supplying taxable goods or services in Korea. The simplified small-business VAT regime is available only to individuals with annual taxable turnover below KRW 80 million, and is not available to a Yuhan Hoesa corporation, which must operate under the general VAT registration and reporting regime.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic tax invoicing through the NTS HomeTax electronic tax invoice system. All VAT tax invoices issued by registered businesses must be electronic tax invoices in the NTS-compliant XML format and transmitted to the NTS e-invoice repository via HomeTax or an NTS-approved API/ERP integration. There is no Latin American-style pre-clearance fiscal printer or digital stamp; anti-fraud controls are implemented through NTS real-time matching of e-tax invoice data, mandatory cash receipt issuance for consumer B2C payments, and reconciliation against periodic VAT returns. Electronic tax invoice data must be transmitted by the statutory date for the relevant VAT filing period.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under Article 11 of the Value-Added Tax Act for goods exported through the Korean customs export procedure and for qualifying services supplied outside Korean territory or otherwise blocked from Korean VAT because the recipient is a non-resident and the service is used outside Korea. For a TikTok MCN agency, zero-rating may be claimed only where the creator representation, content production, advertising, or agency services are performed for a non-resident client, the place of supply is outside Korea, the service is not consumed by or targeted at Korean domestic users in a manner that creates Korean VAT exposure, and the consideration is received in foreign currency through an authorized Korean foreign exchange bank. Services involving the management, promotion, or monetization of Korean creators within Korea, or services consumed by Korean resident clients, are subject to the standard 10% VAT rate.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korean Customs Export Declaration approved by the Korea Customs Service, showing HS code, quantity, and FOB value
Commercial invoice and, where applicable, an export sales contract
Bill of Lading for sea freight or Master Air Waybill for air freight
Foreign Exchange Bank Certificate of Purchase/Settlement of Export Proceeds issued by the Korean bank that received the foreign currency remittance

For digital creator services with no customs declaration: non-resident service contract, platform payout reports from TikTok Creator Payout and Wise B2B, proof of non-resident client status, and service performance evidence such as campaign deliverables, creator reports, and usage or consumption evidence outside Korea
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS scrutinizes the export declaration, logistics evidence, electronic tax invoice trail, foreign exchange settlement records, and service performance documentation. If export proceeds are not received within the statutory 18-month foreign exchange repatriation period, or if any customs, foreign exchange, or service export document is forged or falsely presented, the zero-rated supply is reclassified as a domestic standard-rated supply. The NTS may retroactively assess 10% VAT plus additional taxes for negligent or fraudulent underreporting under the Framework Act on National Taxes and the Value-Added Tax Act, require refunds to be immediately repaid with interest, impose penalty surcharges, and refer serious cases for criminal enforcement under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) as central bank; Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) as principal foreign exchange policy authority; delegated to designated foreign exchange banks under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Republic of Korea operates a liberalized but notification-driven foreign exchange system. The Korean won is convertible for most current account transactions, including trade settlements and service/business payments, under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA). Capital account operations, however, remain subject to a negative-list system requiring prior or post reporting, bank confirmation, or registration depending on the character of the flow. Inward foreign direct investment must be reported under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (FIPA) and registered with a designated foreign exchange bank or Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) before capital is remitted. Dividends, royalties, and legitimate current account payments are generally remittable without substantial restriction after tax clearance and submission of the supporting transactional documents. A statutory export proceeds surrender requirement exists in the sense that exporters must collect proceeds within a stipulated period; however, mandatory conversion of foreign currency into won is limited to specified service categories and crisis measures. The Bank of Korea may temporarily require surrender during external stress, but in ordinary circumstances exporters may retain receipts in foreign currency accounts. Practical frictions appear in foreign exchange bank due diligence, requiring underlying contracts, real-use certificates, and customs declarations, rather than absolute convertibility denial.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Article 14 of FETA and related notices, exporters must collect export proceeds within 6 months from the date of customs clearance unless a longer period is approved by the Bank of Korea or a designated foreign exchange bank. In ordinary conditions, there is no mandatory conversion ratio for broadly eligible export receipts; companies may maintain proceeds in foreign currency deposit accounts at domestic banks. However, the Minister of Economy and Finance, upon consultation with the Bank of Korea, may impose a temporary surrender obligation of up to 50% of export receipts during a balance-of-payments crisis. For cross-border MCN service revenue from TikTok, the bank may classify the receipts as service export income and require invoices, settlement statements, and proof of the underlying creator representation contract.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Investment Capital Deposit Account and Basic Operational KRW Account
Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account
Foreign Investor Share Capital Trust Account and Domestic Operations Account
Inbound Investment Proceeds Account and Common Operational Foreign Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Regulatory viability is Low. Foreign fintech EMI providers such as Wise and Airwallex do not hold a Korean banking license under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act and cannot independently service a Korean-domiciled entity for statutory capital account reporting. They may be used as supplementary cross-border settlement rails for creator payouts only if the Korean entity also maintains a domestic won account with a Tier-1 local bank for tax reporting and capital verification. Direct onboarding of a Korean LLC on an overseas EMI in lieu of a local corporate bank account is legally barred for FDI capital injection and foreign exchange registration.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively required. Under the Financial Transactions Reports Act and standard Korean banking practice, the statutory director or a properly authorized local representative must appear at the bank branch for KYC interview and identity verification. Remote consular notarization is acceptable to validate the power of attorney, but it does not replace the in-branch appearance of the named representative. A completely remote account opening for a foreign-owned Korean LLC is not realistic unless the bank has already completed an onshore site visit and the compliance team has verified the directors biometric data through an approved face-to-face process.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear beneficial ownership chain for a foreign-owned Korean LLC with layered offshore holding entities or nominee shareholders.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete organizational chart with each shareholder layer, authenticated register of beneficial owners, certified passport copies of all ultimate natural persons, apostilled certificates of incorporation for every legal entity in the chain, signed beneficial ownership declarations, corporate resolution granting account opening authority, and a written commercial rationale for the cross-border TikTok MCN structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial seed capital injection arrives as a personal wire from a foreign individual rather than as a documented foreign direct investment remittance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: KOTRA or designated bank foreign investment report filing, foreign investment registration certificate, confirmation of inward investment remittance from the bank, source of wealth documentation such as tax returns and audited financial statements, 12-month bank statements of the remitter, and a board resolution recording the share issuance and capital contribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business purpose mismatch where a creator MCN agency classified under ISIC 7310 receives recurring cross-border platform settlements that may appear as anonymous digital service fees.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed talent representation agreements, TikTok Global Solutions commercial contracts, creator payout statements from TikTok showing fee calculations, service fee invoices, tax clearance certificates, corporate income tax returns demonstrating arm's length revenue, and a documented flow of funds between the Korean entity and overseas creator channels.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Name screening sensitivity caused by the global scope of the company name and potentially matching a sanctions or adverse media record of a beneficial owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full passport or national ID copies of every director and shareholder, signed PEP and sanctions questionnaire, negative independent database screening reports, adverse media verification letters, proof of no sanctioned territory operations, source of wealth and economic substance evidence, and an undertaking to provide ongoing transactional monitoring access.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound foreign direct investment must be reported under FIPA to KOTRA or a designated foreign exchange bank before the remittance is made. The investor should open a foreign-investor capital deposit account at a Tier-1 Korean bank, wire the capital via SWIFT MT103 with the appropriate foreign exchange purpose code for investment funds, and ensure the remitter name matches the actual foreign investor. After the remittance is received, the bank issues the foreign investment registration certificate. Capital verification is completed by reconciling the foreign investment report, remittance advice, bank receipt confirmation, foreign investment registration certificate, and the subsequent corporate registration filing with the Korean court registry. Funds held in the capital deposit account cannot be used for general operations until the registration process is complete and the funds are formally transferred to the operating account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For outbound trade and creator disbursements, the Korean MCN agency should use SWIFT MT103 for high-value service payments to overseas creators, commercial letters of credit for physical goods or production contracts requiring documentary assurance, and documentary collections for invoice-backed agency fee settlements. Every outbound payment must be supported by an underlying contract, invoice, talent representation agreement, and a designated foreign exchange transaction report where required. TikTok inbound payouts to the Korean entity should be recorded as service export proceeds with matching platform settlement statements. For performance bonuses and international talent guarantees, standby letters of credit may be used in conjunction with the operating bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot and deliverable forward contracts up to one year with proven underlying service or trade exposure in accordance with FETA
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on the Korean won for non-resident counterparties and eligible hedgers when settled against onshore spot rates
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for long-term foreign currency borrowing where a recognized underlying debt exposure exists
FX option strategies such as collars and cost-reducing options with real foreign exchange risk documentation and no speculative open position
Renewable forward rollover arrangements only where the underlying commercial exposure remains unpaid and is reverified by the bank

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: National Corporate Income Tax Return and self-assessment of corporate income tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) through the HomeTax electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the close of the fiscal year; for a December 31 fiscal year-end the statutory unextended deadline is March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file triggers an additional tax of 20% of the unpaid tax for non-filing or 10% of the under-reported tax; fraudulent non-filing or fraudulent underreporting triggers a 40% penalty; unpaid corporate tax accrues delinquent interest at 0.022% per day (approximately 8.03% per annum). Persistent delinquency permits asset seizure by the NTS and, after repeated warning, cancellation of the business registration for the company, which functionally terminates formal corporate trading activity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Tax Surcharge return and payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent local government (si/gun/gu) through the Local Tax Integrated System (WeTax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after the close of the fiscal year; for a December 31 fiscal year-end the statutory deadline is April 30 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing is penalized with a 20% non-filing penalty on the unpaid local income tax, a 10% under-declaration penalty, and delinquent interest at 0.022% per day. Continued non-payment enables the local government to seize bank accounts and real property, and prolonged delinquency can lead to cancellation of the local tax registration and closure of the business for administrative purposes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual members meeting and adoption of annual financial statements with statutorily maintained minute book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company registered office; no annual government filing is made for this item, but meeting minutes must be kept at the registered office and produced upon request by members or the court
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the close of each fiscal year under the Korean Commercial Act; for a December 31 fiscal year-end the annual members meeting must be held by March 31, though the Articles of Incorporation may permit a period up to six months where necessary for an external audit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the annual members meeting within the statutory period subjects the responsible directors and company representatives to an administrative fine; the Commercial Act enables fines of up to KRW 10 million for non-compliance with meeting and minute-book duties. No immediate strike-off occurs, but a prosecutor, creditor, or interested party may petition the court to dissolve a dormant or deadlocked company after prolonged non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External audit report prepared by a licensed CPA auditor and delivery to members and the Financial Supervisory Service (when the statutory audit threshold is crossed)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Securities and Futures Commission and Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through the audit report filing system; a copy is also presented to the annual members meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The auditor must deliver the final independent audit report to the company at least two weeks before the annual members meeting; the company must file the adopted audit report with the Financial Supervisory Service within two weeks after the annual members meeting. For a December 31 fiscal year-end, this normally occurs by late March or early April in the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an external auditor or to file the audit report when required under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies subjects the company and its responsible directors to fines of up to KRW 50 million; the Securities and Futures Commission may order an audit and publicly disclose the violation. If the audit report is not presented, the financial statements cannot be validly approved at the members meeting, profit distributions become unlawful, and repeated violations may result in criminal sanctions and director disqualification.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Semi-annual Value-Added Tax returns covering each VAT reporting period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) through the HomeTax electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar fiscal year, the first-half VAT period (January 1 to June 30) must be filed and paid by July 25; the second-half VAT period (July 1 to December 31) must be filed and paid by January 25 of the following year. A company with a non-calendar fiscal year uses the 25th day immediately following the close of each six-month VAT period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing results in a 10% penalty on the unpaid VAT, while underdeclared VAT attracts a 10% underreporting penalty and unpaid VAT accrues delinquent interest at 0.022% per day. Persistent non-filing permits the competent tax office to cancel the business registration and close the place of business for VAT purposes, preventing the issuance of electronic tax invoices and enabling retrospective VAT collection.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Korean Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, a Yuhan Hoesa must appoint a licensed independent CPA auditor when total assets at the immediately preceding fiscal year-end exceed KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9 million at current exchange rates). There is no separate compulsory audit trigger based solely on turnover or headcount for a private Korean limited company. A Yuhan Hoesa is also subject to mandatory external audit if it is designated as a public-interest business entity under the Act, if it issues public securities, if the Securities and Futures Commission has ordered an external audit, or if the company voluntarily assumes an audit obligation under its Articles of Incorporation or a third-party financing agreement. Companies below the KRW 12 billion asset threshold are generally exempt from a statutory external audit but may still require a CPA review or certified compilation for tax and lending purposes.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP) for non-public private companies; Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) may be applied voluntarily by a private limited company or mandatorily when the company is listed or designated as a public-interest entity. A statutory audit opinion must be issued in the Korean language under the applicable Korean accounting framework, and if the global TikTok MCN parent group requires IFRS-based consolidated reporting, K-IFRS would be the appropriate reporting basis.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not maintain a public annual UBO register for a private Yuhan Hoesa. The statutory obligation is continuous: the company must maintain an accurate register of members at the registered office and must record every transfer of a membership interest before the transfer becomes effective against the company. There is no annual UBO confirmation return to a Korean registry, but any reportable shareholding or membership-interest change, including the acquisition by a foreign investor of 10% or more of the company's capital, must be reported through the foreign-investment procedure. Under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, a foreign investor must file a Foreign Investment Report with KOTRA or a designated foreign exchange bank within 30 days after the acquisition or capital contribution; qualifying investments receive a Foreign Investment Registration Certificate. A subsequent transfer that changes the foreign ownership percentage must likewise be updated in the foreign-investment record within 30 days from the date of the transfer.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 - USD 1,500 per year for a serviced registered office and legal process agent; USD 1,500 - USD 4,500 per year for a full corporate secretarial agent covering meeting preparation, minutes, statutory register maintenance, and annual filing calendar management.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - USD 20,000 for a Korean statutory audit of a small to mid-size limited company with straightforward creator payout flows; USD 3,000 - USD 7,000 for a CPA review or agreed-upon procedures engagement when the statutory audit threshold is not crossed.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 9% to 24% progressive national corporate income tax; 9% on tax base up to KRW 200 million, 19% on tax base above KRW 200 million up to KRW 20 billion, 21% on tax base above KRW 20 billion up to KRW 300 billion, 24% on tax base exceeding KRW 300 billion
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Foreign-invested enterprises in Free Economic Zones may enjoy corporate tax holidays of 100% for 5 years and another 50% for 2 years on qualifying businesses; R&D tax credits of up to 40-50% on eligible innovation and creative technology expenditures; special surtax reduction for small and medium enterprises under the Special Tax Treatment Control Act; technology-transfer income may be excluded partially; local income tax surcharge of 10% of national corporate income tax remains payable unless separately exempted

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Base and Tax Calculation Schedule (primary corporate income tax return) and related international transaction disclosure schedules; filed electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax system at www.hometax.go.kr
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual for the fiscal year; quarterly interim prepayments are due where prior-year tax base exceeds statutory thresholds
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months from the fiscal year-end; for a December year-end the statutory deadline is March 31 of the following year; an extension of up to one month is available when the return is prepared and certified by a licensed tax accountant

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report gross revenue from creator incubation, MCN agency commissions, TikTok platform payout sharing, live-stream tips, brand sponsorship, and management fees less allowable expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident foreign corporation with a Korean place of business must recognize Korean-source income on an accrual basis in this box; offshore settlement received from a foreign TikTok related entity cannot be omitted merely because the contract is signed outside Korea; full reconciliation of Wise B2B and TikTok Creator Payout remittances to declared revenue is mandatory to avoid an omission penalty

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Non-Taxable Income and Non-Deductible Expense Adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add back non-deductible expenses such as excessive entertainment, penalties, fines, and non-statutory reserves; subtract non-taxable income and tax-exempt income; reconcile book net income to tax accounting income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany charges from the TikTok group are deductible only to the extent they are at arm's length, supported by valid invoices, and substantively performed; royalties paid to foreign group licensors require prior withholding tax; if the 22% withholding was not applied, the expense is disallowed and added back on this box

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Tax Base after Loss Carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute the final taxable base after applying statutory loss carryforward deductions, foreign exchange adjustments, and previous-year adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a foreign corporation PE, this box must contain only Korean-source profits attributable to the PE under the Corporate Income Tax Act and the relevant tax treaty business-profit article; treaty income apportionment methodology and function, asset, and risk analysis must be documented before claiming allocation of non-Korean overhead to reduce Korean tax

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the progressive statutory rates to the tax base; subtract tax credits including foreign tax credit, R&D credit, and temporary investment credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident foreign corporations must substantiate foreign tax credit claims with official foreign tax receipts; if a tax treaty reduces Korean-source income tax, the treaty reduction must be claimed through the statutory treaty application procedure, not simply shown as a credit on this box; unsubstantiated treaty credits will be reversed with interest and penalties

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Domestic or Foreign Corporation Status and Tax Representative
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identify the taxpayer as either a domestic corporation or a foreign corporation; enter country of head office, foreign registration number, and resident tax representative details
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign corporation must mark the foreign-corporation declaration and appoint a resident tax representative acceptable to the National Tax Service before filing; failure to maintain a valid tax representative constitutes a fatal compliance defect that can elevate withholding rates, suspend treaty benefits, and expose the offshore head office to direct collection actions

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: File the integrated international transaction schedule detailing all transactions with foreign related parties including licensing, management fees, creator contracts, platform revenue sharing, and brand-referral commissions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Every transaction with ByteDance or TikTok group entities in excess of false-invoice thresholds must be disclosed; if the aggregate value exceeds KRW 10 billion for the fiscal year, integrated Master File and Local File documentation must be submitted with or before the filing; bank remittance amounts from Wise B2B and TikTok payouts must match the schedule values line-by-line

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty is 20% of the unpaid tax where no return is filed; understatement penalty is 10% of the deficient tax for ordinary mistakes and 40% for fraudulent or wilful concealment; daily late-payment interest accrues at 0.022% per day on unpaid national corporate income tax; the local income tax surcharge adds 10% of the national penalty amount; false intercompany invoices expose the taxpayer to additional penalties of up to 2% of the supply value; wilful tax evasion triggers criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act with imprisonment up to 5 years or fines up to three times the evaded tax

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wHT_rate: 22% on gross outbound dividends paid by a Korean corporation to a non-resident corporate shareholder, composed of a 20% national withholding tax plus a 2% local income tax surcharge; treaty rates may reduce this but only if the recipient is the beneficial owner and the DTA application is approved before payment
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a bilateral double taxation treaty, the Korean payer must submit the non-resident domestic-source income treaty application form to the district tax office before remittance; the attachment package must include a Tax Residency Certificate issued by the foreign tax authority, a detailed beneficial ownership statement with corporate organization charts, proof that the foreign recipient has economic substance such as employees, premises, and real business activities, and underlying dividend board resolutions or royalty agreements; if the treaty application is not accepted before remittance, the 22% statutory rate must be withheld and the non-resident may file a refund claim with the National Tax Service within three years, attaching the same TRC and substance evidence; treaty relief is denied if the Korean entity is a mirror shell or conduit for tax avoidance under the adjustment of International Taxes Act anti-abuse doctrine
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding is 22% on outbound interest and royalties to non-residents, consisting of 20% national and 2% local surtax; applicable DTA rates generally range between 0% and 15% depending on the treaty partner, but a valid TRC, beneficial ownership certificate, and substantive business-purpose evidence must be filed before remittance; royalties for digital content, TikTok trademarks, and creator-management software licenses are scrutinized against arm's-length valuation and Korean VAT reverse-charge requirements

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 10 billion in aggregate international transactions with foreign related parties per fiscal year triggers mandatory preparation and filing of integrated Transfer Pricing Local File and Master File with the National Tax Service; Country-by-Country Report filing is separately required when the ultimate parent group has consolidated annual revenue above KRW 1 trillion
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not operate a formal ESR or CIGA filing regime, but economic substance is essential through the related-controlled-tax-transaction arm's-length doctrine, the beneficial-ownership requirement for treaty relief, and the broad anti-abuse and substance-over-form rules under the Adjustment of International Taxes Act; for MCN agency activities, the core income-generating activities of creator scouting, contract negotiation, campaign management, payment collection, sponsorship sourcing, and platform analytics must be performed by Korean decision-makers and employees in Korea; a Korean entity without local staff, operational control, or profit-paying capacity is treated as a conduit shell, its transactions are recharacterized at arm's length, and its members lose limited-liability protection for resulting tax fraud

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Omission of Offshore Creator Payout Revenues
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Systematically omitting TikTok Creator Payout receipts, live-stream gifts, and platform settlement amounts from the Korean corporate tax return by moving creator revenues to foreign shell bank accounts, classifying agency commissions as non-taxable loans, or using nominee payout accounts while Korean staff and management perform all creator-value functions in Korea
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Article 3: imprisonment up to 5 years or a fine not exceeding three times the illegal tax evaded; National Tax Service adds a 40% fraudulent understatement penalty on the omitted corporate income tax, a 0.022% daily late-payment interest charge on the deficiency, and a 10% local income tax surcharge
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly instigate the offshore revenue concealment are jointly and severally liable for the corporation's unpaid tax and penalties through veil piercing; the National Tax Service may issue a travel ban or blacklisting order, attach personal bank accounts and real property, and criminal conviction carries imprisonment of up to 5 years

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Non-Compliance / Missing Intercompany Documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare and submit the integrated Local File and Master File despite KRW 10 billion or more of related-party international transactions with ByteDance or TikTok group entities, or pricing creator representation fees and platform revenue share below arm's length so that Korean taxable profits are artificially moved to zero- or low-tax offshore affiliates
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of International Taxes Act Articles 4 and 5 permit the National Tax Service to reassess controlled transactions at arm's length; failure to present required integrated documentation triggers a documentation penalty and a 10% penalty on the unsubstantiated understated tax base, or 40% where false documents are submitted; daily 0.022% late-payment interest is added to the resulting deficiency
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve false transfer prices, backdated agreements, or sham invoices for services never rendered are personally liable for the reassessed tax and penalties under the principle of punitive veil piercing; civil asset restitution includes freezing personal property, and the criminal route under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act may impose imprisonment for up to 5 years in addition to fines and travel restrictions

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Entity and Treaty Abuse for Dividend Under-Withholding
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a mailbox foreign holding company as the nominal shareholder of the Korean operating entity solely to claim a reduced DTA withholding rate on dividends and royalties, while no substantive management, financing, or decision-making occurs in that shell jurisdiction; falsifying Tax Residency Certificates or beneficial ownership declarations to escape the 22% statutory dividend WHT
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Treaty avoidance is rebutted under the Adjustment of International Taxes Act Article 4, the Framework Act on Taxes Article 47-3, and limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose-test clauses in Korea's tax treaties; the National Tax Service re-imposes the full 22% withholding, adds a 40% fraud penalty, accrues daily interest, and exposes officers to criminal fraud sanctions when the conduit structure is used to evade tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who designs or operates the conduit shareholder chain cannot hide behind the LLC corporate veil; the National Tax Service will pierce the entity to collect unpaid withholding tax and penalties from personal assets, will impose a travel ban after certifying the director as a bad-faith tax debtor, and criminal prosecution can result in imprisonment of up to 5 years, additionally revoking the company's access to future tax clearance and cross-border payment licenses
